landscape.label: Cost by Service
landscape.title: What other drain services cost
landscape.speak: Nationally, here's what other drain services run. Basic snaking, one hundred dollars to two hundred fifty dollars. A video camera inspection, one hundred fifty dollars to four hundred dollars. An after-hours emergency call, one hundred fifty dollars to five hundred dollars and up. A motorized auger, two hundred dollars to three hundred fifty dollars. And hydro jetting, three hundred dollars to six hundred dollars.
landscape.say: Nationally, here's what other drain services run. Basic snaking, $100 to $250. A video camera inspection, $150 to $400. An after-hours emergency call, $150 to $500 and up. A motorized auger, $200 to $350. And hydro jetting, $300 to $600.

landscape.label: Cost by Drain
landscape.title: Cost by drain type
landscape.speak: It also depends on which drain. A kitchen sink runs about one hundred dollars to two hundred fifty dollars, a bathroom sink or shower one hundred dollars to two hundred twenty-five dollars, a toilet one hundred twenty-five dollars to three hundred dollars, a floor or laundry drain one hundred fifty dollars to three hundred fifty dollars, and a main sewer line two hundred fifty dollars to six hundred dollars and up.

landscape.label: What Moves the Price
landscape.title: What moves your price

cards.name: How bad the clog is
cards.desc: A slow sink vs. a fully blocked main line

cards.name: Method
cards.desc: Hand snake, cable machine, camera or jetting

landscape.say: What moves your price? How bad the clog is. Where it is, and how easy it is to reach. The method it takes, from a hand snake to a cable machine, a camera, or hydro jetting. And timing: many companies charge one and a half to two times the normal rate after hours.

landscape.label: DIY vs. Pro
landscape.title: DIY vs. calling a pro

rows.label: Deeper clogs
rows.b: Cable machine clears it back to the main

rows.label: Keeps coming back
rows.b: Camera shows what's in the line

landscape.speak: Should you try it yourself first? A plunger costs five dollars to fifteen dollars, and a hand auger twenty dollars to fifty dollars. They're fine for shallow clogs. Chemical drain cleaners can open a small clog, but they're hard on older pipes. For grease and roots, you need a cable machine or hydro jetting. And if a clog keeps coming back, a camera shows what's really in the line.
landscape.say: Should you try it yourself first? A plunger costs $5 to $15, and a hand auger $20 to $50. They're fine for shallow clogs. Chemical drain cleaners can open a small clog, but they're hard on older pipes. For grease and roots, you need a cable machine or hydro jetting. And if a clog keeps coming back, a camera shows what's really in the line.

landscape.label: Signs of Trouble
landscape.title: Signs a drain needs cleaning
items: Sink fills while the dishwasher runs
Sewer smell near a floor drain
Water comes up during a storm
Clog is back a week after plunging
landscape.note: One slow fixture usually means a local clog. Several at once usually means the main line.
landscape.say: Watch for the warning signs: water draining slowly, the sink filling while the dishwasher runs, a gurgling toilet or tub, a sewer smell near a floor drain, water coming up during a storm, or a clog that's back a week after you plunged it. One slow fixture usually means a local clog. Several at once usually means the main line.
